purpose: Use already-published absolute twilight photometry to test whether the frozen Level-B v3/MYSTIC-derived sky model is grossly inconsistent with real twilight brightness while preserving the untouched Izaña/Pandora holdout boundary.

source.paper: Koomen et al., Measurements of the Brightness of the Twilight Sky, JOSA 42(5), 353-356 (1952)

frozenSelection.selectionReason: All cells lie inside the frozen Level-B physical geometry box. H=-3 and H=-6 are retained to stay well inside the paper's photometric regime; later low-brightness rows are deliberately excluded from the primary benchmark.

geometryMapping.paperP: altitude of sky point above horizon
geometryMapping.paperZ: bearing from the direction of the Sun

evaluation.primaryAbsoluteDiagnostic: For every support-admitted cell, compare ln(observed cd/m2) with the union of certified full-AOD photopic outer bounds over native plus four frozen aerosol scenarios.
evaluation.absoluteMissLog: 0 if observed log luminance lies inside the scenario/AOD union outer interval, otherwise the signed distance to the nearest union boundary.
evaluation.primaryShapeDiagnostic: Report the observed H=-6 versus H=-3 log-luminance decline at matched P,Z. A paired same-AOD/scenario certified shape bound is required before any formal shape PASS/FAIL claim.
evaluation.reasonNoFormalPassFail: The 1952 photometer was described as photopic-sensitivity and photometrically calibrated, but the exact modern CIE response/covariance and contemporaneous AOD are unavailable. This benchmark can reveal strong inconsistency or broad consistency, not replace modern strict validation.
